back: Simple random, convenience, systematic, quota, stratified.
Discrete: countable values. Continuous: any value in a range (measured).
Population: the whole group being studied. Sample: a subset used to draw conclusions about the population.
Every possible sample of the chosen size is equally likely (e.g. number the population and use a random number generator).
Choose every $k$th member from a list, where $k = \frac{\text{population size}}{\text{sample size}}$, starting at a random point within the first $k$.
Both fill proportional groups. Stratified selects **randomly** within each stratum; quota selects non-randomly (e.g. whoever is available) until each quota is met.
Choosing members that are easy to reach. Quick and cheap, but likely to be biased.

front: Discrete or continuous: shoe size, time to run 100 m, number of siblings, mass?
back: Shoe size, siblings: discrete (separate values). Time, mass: continuous (measured).
